data.name: Ghailum
data.gender_notes: Ghailum is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who sets free, liberator. This name is derived from the Arabic root 'gh-l-m', which means 'to release, set free, or liberate'. In Islamic history, the name Ghailum is associated with various figures who have been instrumental in freeing their communities from oppression and tyranny. The name Ghailum carries the meaning “Liberator” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ghailum usually hope their child will grow to embody liberator and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of freedom and liberation in Islam.
data.etymology: Ghailum belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Liberator.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghailum total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ghailum carries a deep resonance in Islamic culture, as it represents the power of liberation and the courage to stand up against injustice. Because of this, it has been given to many prominent figures in Islamic history who have led movements for freedom, such as Ghailum ibn Rib'i, the founder of the Rwabvu resistance movement against European colonization in East Africa in the late 19th century. Additionally, the name can be found in folktales and literary works as a symbol of heroism and valour.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Ghailum is a reminder of the Islamic belief in the importance of setting free the oppressed and standing up for justice. This can manifest in various aspects of life, such as fighting against societal or personal injustices, freeing oneself from mental or spiritual shackles, and striving for the broader emancipation of all human beings. The name is also a tribute to the belief in the transformative power of Allah's mercy to free individuals from the bondage of sin and the cycle of ignorance and error.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the name 'Ghailum' as the title of a Berber leader in the Maghreb in the late 14th century.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun describes Ghailum as a powerful Berber ruler who controlled parts of present-day Algeria and Tunisia.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi mentions 'Ghali ibn Ibrahim al-Ghaili' as the Mamluk Sultan of Egypt in 1422. The name Ghailum carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi records that Ghali, also known as Ghailum, was a Mamluk Sultan who ruled Egypt for a short period of time.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic name Ghailum is gaining popularity in modern times across various platforms. It is frequently used in social media platforms, particularly in Muslim communities where people share and discuss their favorite Islamic names. Ghailum is also a popular choice for parents looking for unique and meaningful names for their babies, as seen on various baby names websites. The name Ghailum is derived from the Arabic language and means 'a heavy rain', which is a significant reminder of Allah's blessings and mercy. The name is also considered to be a rare and beautiful choice in the contemporary Islamic naming tradition.
